messages:
support-engineer: FYI — we've received a handful of high-severity customer tickets and an alert: sustained 5xx on hosted /v1/generate after this morning's deploy (deploy-82). Errors started ~08:23 UTC, current error rate ~6% for top route. stack traces attached in logs.
incident-bot: ALERT: hosted-api /v1/generate error rate >5% (30m window). Top error: 502 upstream reset. See: https://alerts.redwood/ALERT-4259
maya_oncall: Oncall here — can you paste a minimal repro? Any correlation to the canary flags or batches?
support-engineer: Repro snippet from customer A (sanitized):

```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"rwd-large","input":"<~3k tokens prompt>","max_tokens":512}'

HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
{"error":"upstream reset: authcache: token_fetch_failed"}
```

Also seeing 504 on long streaming requests with long-tail latency before the reset.
sam_devex: We rolled a canary flag earlier this morning: route_rank_v2=true for 10% traffic and authcache_ttl lowered from 30s->5s in canary. Both changes went with deploy-82.
alex_infra: Correlating logs — gateway shows repeated 502s with upstream error: "rpc: connection reset by peer" to auth-proxy instances. Auth-proxy logs show token fetch storms: many concurrent cache misses causing outbound KMS auth calls to spike and intermittent upstream timeouts.
ops-oncall: If authproxy is overwhelmed, we should throttle token refreshes. Can we revert the authcache_ttl immediately for canary? ops team, can we add a temporary shedder rule to drop new long-running streams into low-priority queue?
eng-lead-jon: Agreed. Immediate mitigation plan:
1) Turn off route_rank_v2 in the canary group (unwind the ranking change) — runflag: rollback route_rank_v2 -> false
2) Restore authcache_ttl to 30s for canary
3) Rollback deploy-82 if error rate doesn't drop in 5 mins
4) Purge authcache shards on edge where token storms observed: `edgectl cache purge --key-prefix auth:token:`
5) Notify customer success and hold new canary flips until postmortem

Command to disable flag (run from control plane):
```
redctl flags set route_rank_v2 --env=canary --value=false --reason="emergency rollback 5xx"
redctl flags set authcache_ttl --env=canary --value=30 --reason="restore ttl to stable"
```

I can run those in 2m unless someone objects.
support-engineer: No objections — please do it. Also adding list of impacted customers: cust-A, cust-B, cust-C (billing-critical). We have screenshots of 5xxs and some billing incidents opened.
pm-olivia: CS informed top-5 customers, offering immediate credits and a status update. Will post templated note once we confirm rollback outcome.
alex_infra: Ran `redctl flags set` — route_rank_v2=false and authcache_ttl=30 set for canary. Watching.
incident-bot: CONFIG_CHANGE: route_rank_v2=false (user: eng-lead-jon) at 4259876575
incident-bot: CONFIG_CHANGE: authcache_ttl=30 (user: eng-lead-jon) at 4259876580
maya_oncall: Error rate dropped to ~1.2% within 3 minutes. 502s reduced, 504s mostly cleared. Still seeing a handful of residual timeouts from older streams.
ops-oncall: I applied a temporary shedder rule to limit concurrent streaming requests per token to 50 on edge pool-7. That should blunt any hot token storms.
support-engineer: Verified with cust-A — requests now succeeding. Repro case no longer returning 502.
eng-lead-jon: Given improvement, hold on full rollback for now. We'll keep canary flagged off and auth ttl restored, and schedule a controlled test tomorrow with telemetry knobs to validate token refresh behavior.
pm-olivia: Sent customer note and offered credits. Customer-success-liz coordinating individual follow-ups.
customer-success-liz: logged credits for cust-A and cust-B, following up with legal for cust-C billing break.
alex_infra: Follow-ups: need a postmortem to track root cause — likely combination of route_rank_v2 changing routing fanout + aggressive authcache ttl causing stampeding token refreshes under long-prompt workload. Suggest adding circuit-breaker on authproxy and backpressure signals from gateway.
maya_oncall: I'll own the incident timeline and initial RCA writeup. Will collect logs, flags diff, and the exact traffic slice. Tentative severity: sev2 -> downgraded to monitoring.
eng-lead-jon: Thanks team. If error rate climbs again, we perform full rollback of deploy-82 with `redctl deploy rollback --id=deploy-82 --force` and notify customers. Closing this thread once postmortem posted.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Error rate returned to baseline. Monitor for 60 minutes before close.
